title: Why Even One Outlier Destroys the Mean

points.heading: The Mean Has Zero Breakdown
points.body: The sample mean is defined as the sum of observations divided by n. If any single observation gets arbitrarily large, the mean becomes arbitrarily large. So the mean fails entirely when even one extreme value is present.

points.heading: The Median Survives Extremes
points.body: The median is the central value in a distribution where equal numbers of values lie above and below. If a minority of observations go to infinity, the median will not be arbitrarily bad. Its breakdown point is one half.

points.heading: When Is the Mean Actually Good?
points.body: The mean is a good estimator only if the data have zero outliers, no skewness, and unimodality. The median is far more insensitive to these departures.

takeaway: Even a single outlier makes the sample mean completely arbitrary, giving it a breakdown point of zero.

Linear or Logistic Regression? Look at Your Outcome

points.heading: The outcome dictates the model
points.body: Regression helps reveal how different factors connect to disease outcomes. Deciding between linear and logistic models depends completely on how you measure your dependent variable.

points.heading: Linear models require continuous data
points.body: In linear regression, the dependent variable must be continuous, such as intraocular pressure or visual acuity. Independent variables may be continuous, binary, or categorical.

points.heading: Logistic models need binary outcomes
points.body: Logistic regression stands out because its dependent variable must be binary, meaning it only allows for two possible outcomes, like yes or no.

points.heading: Comparing the effect metrics
points.body: Linear regression reports coefficients showing unit changes in the outcome. Logistic regression expresses predictor effects using an odds ratio to compare relative odds of the event.

takeaway: Linear regression requires a continuous outcome, whereas logistic regression demands a binary dependent variable.
